predictions.experiment: Share of the gap problems in the budget part
predictions.recipe: Gap: in studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json, gap problems are rows with t2_right true and t1_right false (null or missing t1_right/t2_right: not a gap problem; cap hits keep their stored t1_right). Define kB = number of rows of studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl with that problem_index, attempt == 0, sample in {0,1,2,3} and score_v3 == 1, and kR the same in studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (cap-hit rows, null score_v3 and missing samples count as not right; a duplicated (problem_index, sample) uses its first row in file order). Assign each gap problem to the first rule that takes it: R1 budget: t1_cap_hit == true. R2 answer-statement: failure_type, lower-cased, contains any of 'format', 'final line', 'garbled', 'rejected', 'changed' (null or missing: not taken). R3 reliability: kB >= 1. R4 capability: kB == 0 and kR >= 2. Otherwise: unassigned. Statistic: (number of gap problems assigned to budget) / (number of gap problems).
predictions.note: Files: rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json; day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (D); day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (E). t1_right/t2_right are stored as ints 0/1, so 'true' is read as == 1 and 'false' as == 0 (bool also accepted); null or missing: not a gap problem. Statistic = budget count / gap count, with R1 = t1_cap_hit is True. n = gap problems; bootstrap over gap problems. kB/kR use the first attempt-0 row per (problem_index, sample), samples 0-3, and count cap-hit rows as not right. These do not affect R1. alt_measured: gap taken as cell == 'rl_only' (the gap text names that cell). It differs only if cell and the right flags disagree. The theory statement says the base capped 'without a loop', but the rule does not test for a loop, and per_problem.json has no loop field, so the script does not test for one.

predictions.experiment: Share of the gap problems in the answer-statement part
predictions.recipe: Gap: in studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json, gap problems are rows with t2_right true and t1_right false (null or missing t1_right/t2_right: not a gap problem; cap hits keep their stored t1_right). Define kB = number of rows of studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl with that problem_index, attempt == 0, sample in {0,1,2,3} and score_v3 == 1, and kR the same in studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (cap-hit rows, null score_v3 and missing samples count as not right; a duplicated (problem_index, sample) uses its first row in file order). Assign each gap problem to the first rule that takes it: R1 budget: t1_cap_hit == true. R2 answer-statement: failure_type, lower-cased, contains any of 'format', 'final line', 'garbled', 'rejected', 'changed' (null or missing: not taken). R3 reliability: kB >= 1. R4 capability: kB == 0 and kR >= 2. Otherwise: unassigned. Statistic: (number of gap problems assigned to answer-statement) / (number of gap problems).
predictions.note: Files and gap as k1. R2 = not budget, and failure_type lower-cased contains 'format', 'final line', 'garbled', 'rejected' or 'changed'. Null or non-string failure_type is not taken. The match is a raw substring test, so a label like 'unchanged...' or 'reformatted' would also match. failure_type is one reader's hand label, set only on rl_only rows. I did not look at the label vocabulary, so I don't know if the substrings hit the labels the theory has in mind ('right answer in a rejected or garbled final line', 'reached gold then changed it'). If the labels use underscores (e.g. 'final_line'), 'final line' will not match. That would lower the share; this is the main risk for this number. alt_measured: gap = cell == 'rl_only'.

predictions.experiment: Fraction of budget-part problems on which a fresh base sample (random matched-norm difference cell, cue) is right
predictions.recipe: Budget-part problems: gap problems (per_problem.json rows with t2_right true and t1_right false; null or missing: not a gap problem) with t1_cap_hit == true in studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. File iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429/answers.jsonl (base + random matched-norm difference, cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500). Take the first row per problem_index in file order. A problem is right if that row has score_v3 == 1; a missing row or null score_v3 counts as wrong, and cap hits keep their stored score_v3. Statistic: right budget-part problems / budget-part problems.
predictions.note: Files: per_problem.json, plus iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429/answers.jsonl, fetched to runs/theory-tests/abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429/answers.jsonl. Its cell is 'rl_random_cue_math500_T1_p1' (model rl_random, prompt_arm cue). The README day1_wdiff table maps this job to random_cue. It has 500 rows, one per problem, and score_v3 is stored on every row. Budget part = gap (t2_right == 1, t1_right == 0) and t1_cap_hit is True. Right = score_v3 == 1 on the first row per problem_index; cap hits keep their stored score. n = budget problems, so the group is small (the theory expects about 16) and the interval is wide. alt_measured: a cap-hit random-cell row counts as wrong even if its stored score_v3 is 1. The script fetches the file with modal volume get if it is missing; if the fetch fails it reports not_computable.

predictions.experiment: Fraction of budget-part problems on which at least one of the 4 independent attempt-0 base_cue samples also hit the cap
predictions.recipe: Budget-part problems as in the previous recipe (gap problems with t1_cap_hit == true in studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json). File studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, rows with attempt == 0 and sample in {0,1,2,3}; a duplicated (problem_index, sample) uses its first row in file order, and missing samples count as not a cap hit. A problem counts if at least one such row has cap_hit == true. Statistic: counted problems / budget-part problems.
predictions.note: Files: per_problem.json and day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Budget part as k6. Counted if any first-row-per-(problem_index, sample) row with attempt == 0 and sample 0-3 has cap_hit True. Missing samples count as no cap hit. Note: the stored T1 sample is not one of these D samples (T1 comes from the S3 r4 run with a different seed), so the samples are independent, as the recipe intends. alt_measured: any row of the problem in D, restarts (attempts 1-2) included, with cap_hit True. A restart only exists after an attempt-0 cap hit, so alt should equal main unless the data break that rule. refuted_by: measured < 0.55 only.

predictions.experiment: Fraction of answer-statement-part problems on which at least one of the base's 4 stored samples is unanswered or repaired by grader v4a
predictions.recipe: Answer-statement-part problems: gap problems (per_problem.json rows with t2_right true and t1_right false; null or missing: not a gap problem) with t1_cap_hit != true whose failure_type, lower-cased, contains any of 'format', 'final line', 'garbled', 'rejected', 'changed', in studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. File studies/rlneurons/results/repair/offline-01/rows.jsonl, rows with model == 'base_cue' (samples 0-3). A problem counts if at least one of its base_cue rows has kind == 'no_answer', or has score_v4 == 1 and score_v3 == 0 (null scores count as 0). Missing rows do not count. Statistic: counted problems / answer-statement-part problems.
predictions.note: Files: per_problem.json and repair/offline-01/rows.jsonl (model == 'base_cue', samples 0-3; all such rows used, no dedupe, and the file has exactly 4 per problem). Answer-statement part = gap, t1_cap_hit not True, failure_type substring match (same substring caveat as k2). Counted if any row has kind == 'no_answer', or (score_v4 == 1 and score_v3 == 0), with null scores counted as 0. score_v4 is the amended grader v4a field, not score_v4_as_specified. The file's kind values are right / finished_wrong / cap_hit / no_answer. alt_measured: kind == 'cap_hit' also counts as 'unanswered', following the experiment title. The group is small (the theory expects about 10), so the interval is wide. The recipe names grader v4a through the stored score_v4, so no grader is re-run.

predictions.note: Files: per_problem.json, day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, and the random-cell answers.jsonl as in k6. Reliability part = gap, t1_cap_hit not True, failure_type matches none of the substrings (null counts as none), kB >= 1.
